newsitem.title: UK: London palladium soars to fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: London palladium soars to fresh highs.

text.p: Palladium prices zoomed up in early European trading on Wednesday, indicated as high as $213/$218 an ounce amid concerns about delayed Russian supplies.
The market had closed at $193/$197 on Tuesday in London.

The rare precious metal, used mainly in electronics, catalytic converters and dentistry, last week fixed at a fresh all-time high level of $196.50. That was its highest level since fixings began in 1989.
Palladium was last at those levels in 1980, long before the twice-daily official fixings began in 1989.
Prices have soared since late last year as supplies from Russia, the world's largest exporter, have failed to reach the market due to delayed supply talks.
Traders said the market was very short and dealers were forced to borrow the metal at very high lease rates or buy on the spot market.
